task_production_rates.name: Seal MDF cut/routed edges (solvent-based)
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. All MDF elements — beam miters, column panel joints, mantel shelf edges, leg edges. Shellac/oil-based sealer applied by small brush to each cut/routed edge. MANDATORY step 1 of MDF two-step prime. NON-NEGOTIABLE. Conditional: substrate=MDF AND substrate_state=SS_BARE. Time depends on element count and complexity.

task_production_rates.name: Seal MDF cut/routed edges (solvent-based)
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. All MDF cut/routed edges inside openings and on door/drawer edges. Shelf dado joints, face frame rabbets, divider joints, back panel rabbets, door edges. Small brush application to each cut edge. MANDATORY step 1 of MDF two-step prime. Conditional: substrate=MDF AND substrate_state=SS_BARE. Built-in MDF has very high edge density — more edges than arch element.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall Edge
task_production_rates.notes: Freehand brush cut-in at wall line from ceiling perspective. ~15% slower than wall cut-in (100 LF/hr) due to overhead arm position. QT2 uses same task at faster pace (~100 LF/hr) due to relaxed precision - minor wavering acceptable if coverage complete. QT4 uses separate TSK_CEIL_CUT_IN_WALL_QT4 task with crisp edge requirement.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall Edge (Premium)
task_production_rates.notes: Careful ceiling brush cut-in for crisp straight line. ~13% slower than wall QT4 cut-in (75 LF/hr) due to overhead position.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall Edge After Ceiling Spray
task_production_rates.notes: Touch-up cut at wall line after removing masking. ~17% slower than wall equivalent (120 LF/hr).

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Ceiling Edge
task_production_rates.notes: Freehand brush cut-in at ceiling line. QT2 uses same task at faster pace (~120 LF/hr) due to relaxed precision - minor wavering acceptable if coverage complete. QT4 uses separate TSK_WALL_CUT_IN_CEILING_QT4 task with crisp edge requirement.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Ceiling Edge (Premium)
task_production_rates.notes: Careful wall brush cut-in for crisp straight line at ceiling edge.

task_production_rates.name: Seal MDF cut/routed edges (solvent-based)
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. ~3 min per riser for edge sealing. Includes stringer cut edges pro-rated. Shellac or oil-based sealer. Conditional: substrate=mdf AND substrate_state=SS_BARE.

task_production_rates.name: Seal MDF cut/routed edges (solvent-based)
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Detail work — shellac or oil-based sealer on all cut/routed edges and profiles. Wainscot has extensive routed profiles creating more edge area than simple trim. Conditional: substrate=mdf AND substrate_state=SS_BARE. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Seal MDF cut/routed edges (solvent-based)
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rate (wall: 60→ceiling: 45). Detail work overhead — shellac/oil sealer on cut/routed MDF edges. Sealer runs/drips from overhead edges. Apply in thin coats. Conditional: substrate=mdf AND substrate_state=SS_BARE. Binary. MANDATORY step 1 of MDF two-step prime.

task_production_rates.name: Seal MDF cut/routed edges (solvent-based)
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Detail work — shellac or oil-based sealer on ALL cut/routed edges and profiles. Board-style MDF walls: factory-milled edges (shiplap overlap, T&G tongue/groove) are cut surfaces requiring sealing. Panel-style MDF walls: routed profiles on rails/stiles. Conditional: substrate=mdf AND substrate_state=SS_BARE. Binary. MANDATORY step 1 of MDF two-step prime — water-based causes irreversible fiber swelling (Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine §2.1, §4.1).

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Ceiling Line
task_production_rates.notes: Angled brush cut-in at ceiling line. WALL PAINTER ESTABLISHES THE CEILING LINE. Freehand cut-in, no tape. Base 100 LF/hr adjusted for QT2 economy pace. Per Production Rate Reference: TSK_CUTIN_CEILING base = 100 LF/hr, QT2 = 130 LF/hr.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Ceiling Line (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.notes: Second coat cut-in at ceiling line. Same technique as first coat.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Trim Edges (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.notes: Cut in wall paint at baseboard, door casing, window casing tape lines. Cut into tape edge for clean reveal. Per Production Rate Reference: TSK_CUTIN_TRIM QT3 = 90 LF/hr; this is faster because cutting to tape.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Trim Edges (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.notes: Second coat cut-in at trim edges. Same technique as first coat.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Trim Edges (Spray Method, Coat 1)
task_production_rates.notes: Cut-in at trim tape lines before spray application. Same brush technique and rate as roll-method cut-in — spray vs roll affects field application, not edge work.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Trim Edges (Spray Method, Coat 2)
task_production_rates.notes: Second coat cut-in at trim edges before spray. Same technique as first coat.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall at Trim Edges (Spray Only)
task_production_rates.notes: Cut-in at trim tape lines for spray-only method. Same brush technique as roll and spray_backroll cut-in. Spray-only limited to QT2-QT3.

task_production_rates.name: Seal MDF cut edges with shellac
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. All MDF cut/routed edges on doors, drawers, and face frames. Small brush application to each cut edge. MANDATORY step 1 of MDF two-step prime. Conditional: substrate=MDF AND substrate_state=SS_BARE. Cabinet doors have 4 edges each — significant edge density. Per SF_BUILTIN_NC_v1 precedent.
